title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 108 (Voting through electronic means)

content.overview: Section 108 is an enabling provision. The Central Government may prescribe the class or classes of companies and the manner in which a member may exercise the right to vote by electronic means. The section itself does not name every company that must provide the facility or set the procedural detail; those are in the rules made under the Act (notably Rule 20 of the Companies (Management and Administration) Rules, 2014, as amended).
content.glance: The Central Government may prescribe the classes of companies and the manner in which members may vote by electronic means. The operative class and procedure are in the rules, not in the section text alone.
content.study:
## Section 108 — voting through electronic means

**The enabling rule.** Section 108 provides that the Central Government may prescribe the class or classes of companies and the manner in which a member may exercise his right to vote by the electronic means.

**What the section does not do.** It does not itself list every company that must offer electronic voting, set member thresholds, define remote e-voting, or prescribe notice, cut-off, agency or scrutiniser procedure. Those matters are left to subordinate legislation.

**Interaction with other provisions.** Where electronic voting applies under the prescribed rules, section 107's show-of-hands default is displaced for the relevant resolution (section 107 itself excepts the case where voting is carried out electronically). Section 109 (poll) remains a separate regime. Postal ballot under section 110 has its own interaction with section 108 for companies that must provide electronic voting.

**Rules (illustrative only; not a verified current consolidation).** Rule 20 of the Companies (Management and Administration) Rules, 2014 has historically required every company which has listed its equity shares on a recognised stock exchange and every company having not less than one thousand members to provide a facility to vote by electronic means, subject to exemptions and conditions in the rule. The precise current class, exemptions and procedure must be checked against the latest official rules and notifications; do not treat a secondary restatement as primary law.

## Apply the provision
- Identify whether the company falls within a class prescribed under section 108 and the applicable rules.
- Do not invent a threshold or procedure as if it were written in section 108 itself.
- Separate the enabling section from Rule 20 (or successor) detail, and from sections 107 and 109.

This note is a focused study aid; the topic remains under source and current-law review.

examples.title: Enabling provision, not a self-contained threshold
examples.body: A student is asked whether every company with 500 members must provide electronic voting under section 108. The correct approach is to state that section 108 only enables the Central Government to prescribe classes and manner; any numerical threshold or class is in the rules, not in the section text. This is an educational illustration, not advice about a real company.

examples.title: Displacement of show of hands
examples.body: Where electronic voting applies under the prescribed rules for a resolution, section 107's show-of-hands default does not decide that resolution, because section 107 itself excepts the case where voting is carried out electronically. This is an educational illustration.

hypotheticals.question: Does section 108 itself require every listed company to provide electronic voting?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 108 is enabling: the Central Government may prescribe the class or classes of companies and the manner of electronic voting. Whether a listed company (or any other company) must provide the facility depends on the rules made under the section. State the section, then the applicable rule, and check current exemptions.

hypotheticals.question: A company provides remote e-voting for a general-meeting resolution. A member argues that the resolution must still be decided on a show of hands under section 107. How should the interaction be analysed?
hypotheticals.analysis: Section 107(1) provides that a resolution is decided on a show of hands unless a poll is demanded under section 109 or the voting is carried out electronically. Where electronic voting applies under section 108 and the rules, the show-of-hands default is displaced for that resolution. Confirm the prescribed class and that electronic voting was the method in use.

misconceptions.trap: Treating a member threshold (for example 1,000 members) as if it were written in section 108 itself.
misconceptions.correction: Section 108 only enables the Central Government to prescribe classes and manner. Any threshold is in the rules and must be checked against the current official text.

misconceptions.trap: Assuming electronic voting and show of hands always run side by side for the same resolution.
misconceptions.correction: Section 107 itself excepts the case where voting is carried out electronically. Where the electronic regime applies, the show-of-hands default is displaced for that resolution.

misconceptions.trap: Confusing section 108 with the full Rule 20 procedure (agency, cut-off, scrutiniser, remote e-voting definitions).
misconceptions.correction: The section is the enabling provision. Procedure and definitions are in the rules; cite them separately and verify the current consolidation.
